It was rebuilt at Book IV step 1 (three PG illustration captions, one of them in Book IX; 7bf2d1b1... -> b0ecf3da...) and at Book VII step 1 (three of Long's footnotes printed flush left; b0ecf3da... -> 7798607d...). Book IX is the book the Book VIII reviewer warned about, because PG line 5628 carries an illustration caption inside it ([Illustration: THE FORUM], standing alone between IX.21 and IX.22). That caption is ALREADY STRIPPED by the filter added at Book IV step 1: IX.21 ends at 'a thing to be afraid of.' and IX.22 begins at '22.'. PG lines 5419-5864 were re-read line by line for every class the earlier rebuilds missed - footnote openers and bodies whether indented or flush left, illustration captions, running heads, page numbers, catchwords, verse and verse citations, in-text Greek - and the result is: eight footnotes (PG 5462, 5515, 5601, 5649, 5680, 5707, 5778, 5858), all indented and all already stripped; no flush-left footnote opener; exactly three standalone flush-left lines in the whole book (the IX. header, the X. header, and the caption at 5628); no running head, no page number; no verse and no verse citation at all; no Greek in the body (every [Greek: ...] span in the range is inside a footnote body). NO REBUILD was made, so no paragraph anywhere in the file changed and no accepted book is reopened.

shall_rule: First book drafted under the rule fixed at Book VIII acceptance (GLOSSARY.md, Voice and form). Three plain futures were rendered without 'shall' (IX.3: 'which shall reach thy heart' -> 'which will reach your heart'; 'when the child shall come out' -> 'when the child comes out'; 'when thy soul shall fall out' -> 'when your soul falls out'). Eight 'shall' are kept, all licensed: six first-person deliberative questions at IX.40, one indirect deliberative question inside Epicurus's reported speech at IX.41, and the emphatic/volitional 'They themselves shall judge' at IX.29, which is offered to the reviewer for confirmation. No second-person 'shall' and no plain-future 'shall' survives.
base_text_defects: IX.34 PG 'their pool souls' (line 5741); Standard Ebooks reads 'poor souls', and Long has 'their poor souls' himself at IX.27 (line 5664). Rendered 'poor souls'. FLAGGED - the one departure from PG's letters in Book IX.
IX.35 PG 'condemned to be bound in never ceasing evil'; SE 'condemned to be found', which says nothing and looks like an eye-skip from 'no power has ever been found'. PG is right and is followed.
IX.35 SE adds a word PG does not have: 'have been done in like form' against PG's 'have been in like form'. PG is followed under D6.

IX.40 PG 'Pray thou: How shall I not desire to be released?'; SE reads 'Another prays:', which breaks the alternation of the man's prayer and Marcus's through all three turns. PG is right and is followed.

IX.29 PG 'insolence and pride' (line 5705); SE 'indolence and pride'. Followed PG, and CLOSED at round 1 in PG's favour on the argument of the meditation rather than on D6 alone. No longer flagged as open.

IX.28 SE prints the section as two typographic paragraphs (breaking before 'Soon will the earth cover us all'), so an automatic count of SE's Book IX paragraphs returns 43. PG prints it whole and 42 is the standard section count. No text differs; the candidate keeps Long's section whole.
flagged_for_reviewer: IX.34 'poor souls' rendered for PG's 'pool souls' - the one place in Book IX where the candidate departs from PG's letters -- RULED THE DRAFTER'S WAY AT ROUND 1 without reservation; SETTLED in continuity.md. The reviewer confirmed by grep that 'poor souls' at IX.27 and 'pool souls' at IX.34 are the ONLY two occurrences of the phrase in the whole PG file, so the internal witness is exact rather than approximate.

IX.29 'insolence' followed from PG against Standard Ebooks' 'indolence' -- CLOSED AT ROUND 1 in favour of PG on grounds stronger than D6, and SETTLED in continuity.md: the meditation is about grandiosity, its final clause answers 'Simple and modest is the work of philosophy' (whose opposite is showy and proud, not lazy and proud), indolence has no antecedent anywhere in the meditation, and 'indolence'/'insolence' is a one-letter confusion of the kind a re-keying produces. Limitation on the record: the reviewer did not consult a Greek text and a reviewer with the Greek could overturn it.

IX.29 'They themselves shall judge' kept as the emphatic/volitional 'shall' -- CONFIRMED AT ROUND 1 and kept; the reviewer would resist 'will' firmly, because the next sentence ('no one has condemned me to imitate them') shows the clause is a dismissal, not a prediction.

review_round_1: review/findings-v1.md (independent reviewer session, 2026-09-12): Accept after corrections; 1 substantive (40.1), 3 minor (1.1, 9.1, 41.1) and 5 optional preferences (1.2, 3.1, 7.1, 28.1, 29.1); 35 of the 42 paragraphs 'No material issue found', every paragraph covered exactly once and in order. Applied in candidate-v2.json via scripts/build_book9_v2.py: 40.1 (IX.40's three corrective turns restored to imperatives -- 'You, pray thus:' / 'You, pray:' / 'You thus:' for v1's 'Do you pray thus:' / 'You pray thus:' / 'You thus:', which in modern English read as a yes/no question and a declarative; the reviewer's proposal taken as offered); 1.1 (Long's 'for' restored at IX.1 in place of an unrecorded fourth 'since', and the continuity sheet corrected from four 'inasmuch as' to three); 9.1 (IX.9 'and in a way, loves' -> 'and, in a way, loves', so 'loves' is not parsed as a verb); 1.2 (IX.1's semicolon restored, the two added definite articles kept). 41.1 is a rule-wording fix, not a text change: ../GLOSSARY.md was widened from 'the deliberative shall of a direct question' to 'a question, direct or indirect', in its own commit BEFORE Book X was drafted, so IX.41's indirect deliberative question is licensed by the rule's letter as well as its spirit. Declined: four optional findings -- 3.1 (IX.3's dropped 'made'; the reviewer's own repair is further from Long and the reviewer preferred the drop recorded to undone, so it is now recorded), 7.1 (IX.7's mixed semicolon and colon; Long's accidentals stand, nothing misdirects, and repointing for evenness alone is unlicensed), 28.1 (IX.28 'do not let yourself also be governed'; the proposed repair drops Long's load-bearing 'also'), 29.1 (IX.29 'All of them drivel.'; 'Drivellers, all of them.' restores a word ruled not current and 'Drivel, all of it.' moves the referent from the men to their talk) -- each recorded as considered in continuity.md. All three flagged decisions were ruled the drafter's way and are settled: IX.34 'poor souls' upheld without reservation, IX.29 'insolence' CLOSED in PG's favour on the argument of the meditation, and IX.29's emphatic 'shall' confirmed. The 'shall' audit passed: eleven in Long, three removed (all IX.3), eight kept and all licensed. The step-1 no-rebuild finding was tested by the STRONGER method the assignment asked for -- an independently written reconstruction of PG lines 5419-5864 diffed word for word against the staged Book IX, not a re-run of the build -- and the only three differences in the whole book are the three documented dagger marks. No second round requested: the one substantive finding is confined to the clause it quotes and every other change is a connective, a comma or a mark of punctuation restored to Long's.
